# Application Documentation

This document provides a detailed analysis of the `App.jsx` source code file, outlining its components, data structures, and functionality.

## File: App.jsx

### Module Overview

`App.jsx` is a React component that renders the main user interface for the Tres Aroma Café website. It manages UI states like scroll position and element visibility for animations, defines static content such as gallery items, menu categories, and operating hours, and structures the overall page layout including header, hero section, story, gallery, rooftop, menu, visit information, and footer.

### State Variables

*   `scrolled`: A boolean state variable that indicates whether the window has been scrolled beyond a certain threshold (40 pixels).
    *   **Type:** `boolean`
    *   **Initial Value:** `false`
    *   **Setter:** `setScrolled`

### Constants

*   `galleryItems`: An array of objects, each representing an item in the café's gallery.
    *   **Structure:**
        *   `title`: String - The title of the gallery item.
        *   `image`: String - The URL or import path for the item's image.
    *   **Example:**
        ```javascript
        [
          { title: 'The Counter', image: counterImage },
          { title: 'Everyday, Every Sip', image: everydayImage },
          // ... more items
        ]
        ```
*   `menuGroups`: An array of objects, defining categories and items for the café's menu.
    *   **Structure:**
        *   `title`: String - The title of the menu group.
        *   `items`: Array of Strings - A list of menu items within the group.
    *   **Example:**
        ```javascript
        [
          { title: 'Signature Coffee', items: ['Tres Aroma House Blend', 'Spanish Latte', 'Salted Caramel Macchiato'] },
          // ... more groups
        ]
        ```
*   `hours`: An array of arrays, representing the operating hours for each day of the week.
    *   **Structure:** Each inner array contains two strings: the day of the week and its corresponding operating time or status.
    *   **Example:**
        ```javascript
        [
          ['Monday', 'Closed for prep'],
          ['Tuesday', '9:00 AM – 11:00 PM'],
          // ... more days
        ]
        ```

### Hooks

*   `useState(false)`: Initializes the `scrolled` state variable to `false`.
*   `useEffect(() => { ... }, [])`: This hook performs side effects in the component.
    *   **Scroll Event Listener:**
        *   Adds a `scroll` event listener to the `window` to update the `scrolled` state based on the scroll position.
        *   The `handleScroll` function sets `scrolled` to `true` if `window.scrollY` is greater than 40, otherwise `false`.
    *   **Intersection Observer:**
        *   Initializes an `IntersectionObserver` to manage scroll entrance animations.
        *   `observerOptions`:
            *   `threshold`: `0.05` - Triggers the callback when 5% of the observed element is visible.
            *   `rootMargin`: `'0px 0px -60px 0px'` - An offset to the root's bounding box.
        *   The observer's callback iterates through `entries`. If an `entry` is `isIntersecting`, it adds the class `active` to the `entry.target` and then stops observing that target to ensure the animation triggers only once.
        *   Selects all elements with the class `reveal` using `document.querySelectorAll('.reveal')`.
        *   Observes each selected element using `revealObserver.observe(el)`.
    *   **Cleanup Function:**
        *   Removes the `scroll` event listener from the `window`.
        *   Stops observing all previously observed `revealElements` using `revealObserver.unobserve(el)`.
    *   **Dependency Array:** An empty array `[]` ensures this effect runs only once after the initial render and the cleanup function runs on unmount.

### Component Structure (`return` statement)

The component renders the following JSX structure:

*   **Header:**
    *   Conditionally applies the `scrolled` class to the `<header>` element.
    *   Contains a navigation bar with a brand logo and name, navigation links (`Story`, `Inside`, `Menu`, `Visit`), and a call-to-action button linking to the Facebook page.
*   **Main Content (`<main id="top">`):**
    *   **Hero Section (`<section className="hero">`):**
        *   Displays a headline, sub-headline, descriptive text, and key attributes/pills.
        *   Includes call-to-action buttons for following updates and getting directions.
        *   Shows meta-information like address, landmark, and planned hours.
        *   Features a hero image.
        *   Elements intended for animation have the `reveal` class and specific fade effects (e.g., `fade-up`, `fade-in`).
    *   **Divider (`<hr className="divider" />`):** A visual separator.
    *   **Story Section (`<section id="story">`):**
        *   Provides details about the café's concept and atmosphere.
        *   Includes descriptive paragraphs and "value items" highlighting core tenets.
        *   Elements have `reveal` classes for animation.
    *   **Gallery Section (`<section id="gallery">`):**
        *   Displays a grid of images with captions.
        *   Uses the `galleryItems` constant to map and render gallery items.
        *   Elements have `reveal` classes for animation.
    *   **Rooftop Section (`<section>`):**
        *   Describes the rooftop area with accompanying text and an image.
        *   Includes a call-to-action button linking to Facebook.
        *   Elements have `reveal` classes for animation.
    *   **Menu Section (`<section id="menu">`):**
        *   Presents the café's menu organized by categories.
        *   Uses `menuGroups` constant to map and render menu sections and items.
        *   Displays two images showcasing food items.
        *   Includes a note about future menu updates.
        *   Elements have `reveal` classes for animation.
    *   **Visit Section (`<section id="visit">`):**
        *   Provides location details, including an embedded Google Map.
        *   Displays the address, landmark, and operating hours in a table format using the `hours` constant.
        *   Elements have `reveal` classes for animation.
*   **Footer (`<footer>`):**
    *   Contains a concluding message, navigation links (back to top, Facebook), and branding information.
    *   Elements have `reveal` classes for animation.

### Imported Assets

*   `logoImage`: `./assets/img/tresaromalogo.jpg`
*   `heroPhoto`: `./assets/img/tresaroma.png`
*   `rooftopPhoto`: `./assets/img/therooftop.png`
*   `counterImage`: `./assets/img/thecounter.png`
*   `treatImage`: `./assets/img/brewsiprelax.png`
*   `everydayImage`: `./assets/img/everydayeverysip.png`
*   `happinessImage`: `./assets/img/mycupofhappiness.png`
*   `food1`: `./assets/img/food1.png`
*   `food2`: `./assets/img/food2.png`

### Code Usage Example

This component is likely the root component of a React application, intended to be rendered within an HTML file's root element (e.g., `ReactDOM.render(<App />, document.getElementById('root'));`).

```jsx
// Assuming this is in your main application entry point (e.g., index.js or App.js)
import React from 'react';
import ReactDOM from 'react-dom/client';
import App from './App'; // Assuming App.jsx is in the same directory or correctly path'd
import './index.css'; // Assuming global CSS is imported here

const root = ReactDOM.createRoot(document.getElementById('root'));
root.render(
  <React.StrictMode>
    <App />
  </React.StrictMode>
);
```

# 1 Tres Aroma Café is a new cozy coffee spot on Tocs Ave., right across from Pleasant Mount School — brewing soon, and built around three things: simple, calm, and a good cup in good company. ## Features & Capabilities * **Dynamic Header:** The navigation header dynamically changes its appearance (adds a 'scrolled' class) when the user scrolls down the page, enhancing visual feedback. * **Animated Content Loading:** Implements an Intersection Observer to trigger fade-in and fade-up animations on various content sections as they enter the viewport, providing a smoother user experience. * **Image Display:** Showcases a variety of images including a logo, hero image, rooftop view, counter area, and food items, contributing to the visual appeal and brand representation. * **Menu Presentation:** Organizes and displays a multi-category menu for coffee, frappes, juices, and snacks, with a note about future updates. * **Location and Hours:** Provides essential information about the café's address, landmark, planned operating hours, and an embedded Google Maps iframe for directions. * **Interactive Elements:** Includes call-to-action buttons linking to the café's Facebook page and Google Maps for directions. * **Responsive Layout:** Utilizes a structure that adapts to different screen sizes, with elements like a two-column hero section and a 2x2 gallery grid. * **Rooftop Section:** Features a dedicated section highlighting a rooftop area with an accompanying image and descriptive text. * **Value Proposition Display:** Showcases core values and mottos of the café through distinct value cards. ## Architecture & Component Breakdown ### `App.jsx` This is the main React component that orchestrates the entire application's UI and behavior. * **State Management:** Uses `useState` to manage the `scrolled` state, which controls the header's appearance. * **Effects:** Employs `useEffect` to: * Add and remove a scroll event listener to update the `scrolled` state. * Initialize and manage an `IntersectionObserver` for element animations. This observer is configured to trigger animations when elements with the class `reveal` enter the viewport. It also handles unobserving elements after their animation has been triggered once. * **Component Structure:** Renders the entire webpage, including: * A sticky header with navigation links and a brand logo. * A hero section with introductory text, call-to-action buttons, and a background image. * A story section detailing the café's concept and values. * A gallery section displaying interior visuals using a 2x2 grid. * A rooftop section with an image and description. * A menu section listing different categories and items. * A visit section including an embedded map and operating hours. * A footer with contact information and social media links. * **Data Structures:** Utilizes arrays of objects (`galleryItems`, `menuGroups`, `hours`) to structure and render dynamic content. ## API & Module Reference ### `App` Component * **Imports:** * `useEffect` from `react`: For managing side effects in functional components. * `useState` from `react`: For managing component state. * Image assets from `./assets/img/`: `logoImage`, `heroPhoto`, `rooftopPhoto`, `counterImage`, `treatImage`, `everydayImage`, `happinessImage`, `food1`, `food2`. * **State Variables:** * `scrolled`: A boolean state variable, initialized to `false`.
